rationale: Inverts the Fidelity ratio so the residual norm becomes the denominator. The form is structurally similar but wrong: the metric is defined as a normalised residual that goes to 0 as the surrogate g approaches the model f, whereas the inverted form diverges in that limit — contradicting the paper's own reading of low fidelity values as good agreement. Perturbs the existing equation in place rather than appending a claim.
ground_truth_description: Fidelity definition: ratio inverted from ||f-g||^2 / ||f||^2 to ||f||^2 / ||f-g||^2, so the metric diverges instead of vanishing under perfect surrogate agreement.

truth.term_role: normalised-residual ratio in the fidelity metric
